summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryoshu Kouda studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Kouda has held researcher positions at Taisho University and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture.

Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Otani University from around 1925 to 1928. He served on the faculty at Otani University and was a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from around 1951 to 1976.

Ryoshu Misaki, a scholar of Buddhist studies, studied at Waseda University from around 1947 to 1951 and later served there as professor emeritus from around 1992 to 2010. His students included Fumimasa Fukui.

Ryoshun Okubo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1973 to 1983. He became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University around 2005 and has served as director of Taimon Kenkyūkai.
Ryoso Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama and held a lectureship at Ryukoku University.

Ryota Nakamura, a Buddhist studies scholar, completed doctoral studies and served as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University. Nakamura has also worked as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.

Ryotai Hatai was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who taught at Kyoto University from 1929 to 1943 and was professor emeritus at Ryukoku University from around 1953 to 1974. He taught Gadjin Nagao and Ryogon Fukuhara.

Ryudo Fujii, an Indology and philosophy scholar, studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii was a JSPS special researcher (around 2001–2003) and held posts at Kokushikan University and Kyoto Women's University.
Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from around 1953 to 1955. He later served as the president of Rissho University from around 1974 to 1993.

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Tanemura has held positions as a specially appointed associate professor at Taisho University, a part-time lecturer at Nishogakusha University, and a researcher at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Ryuichi Abe studied at Keio, SAIS, Taisho, and Columbia. He was a professor at Columbia (~1991–2003) and became Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard around 2003.

Ryuichi Kogachi is a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo from 1989 to 1999. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto University from around 1999 to 2002 and held a post at its Research Centre for the Cultural Sciences.
Ryuichi Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a guest lecturer at Chisan Denpoin and as a researcher at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Ryujo Yamada was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at Tohoku University (professor ~1925–1953), Ryukoku University (~1953–1968), and Musashino University (~1968–1974).
Ryuken Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Ryusei Keira is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Keira studied at the University of Lausanne through 2003 under doctoral supervisor Tom J. F. Tillemans and committee members Shoryu Katsura and Georges Dreyfus.

Ryushin Uryuzu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from around 1951 to 1961. He was a professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1974 to 1998 and held a post at the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Center.
Ryusho Onami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taishun Mibu and served as a lecturer at Taisho University.

Ryuta Kikutani is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at Kyoto University's Hakubi Center/Faculty of Letters from around 2015 to 2020 and served as an expert researcher at Tohoku University.

Indologist Ryutaro Tsuchida studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg, where Wilhelm Rau supervised his doctoral work. He later served as professor at the University of Tokyo from around 1989 to 2012.
